notice: SYNTHETIC TEST CONTENT. These fictional policies are not real company guidance.

metadataColumns.description: Reuse SharePoint's built-in Department text column. Fixture values are CorpNet, HR, Finance and IT.
Semicolon-delimited text tags; not a Managed Metadata field.

sites.title: CorpNet Search PoC - Corporate Hub
sites.description: Isolated synthetic corporate hub for a four-site Copilot Studio search proof of concept.

pages.title: Welcome to the synthetic CorpNet
paragraphs: This is the central entry point for the fictional Northstar Demo Collective. Every page and document in this test estate is synthetic.
HR, Finance and IT each have a separate SharePoint site collection with their own pages, libraries, policies and permissions. Departmental sites are not folders or pages inside this site.
Use the department directory to choose a site. A central search agent should support questions across the approved sites without bypassing their permissions.

pages.title: Department directory
paragraphs: HR owns induction, annual leave and people policies. Finance owns expenses, purchasing and payment policies. IT owns devices, access and technical support.
A new starter may need information from both HR and IT. Do not assume that the employee's home department is the only site they may search.
Ask a narrower question or select a department when multiple policies have similar titles. Access to this directory does not grant access to any departmental content.

sections.heading: Corporate help
paragraphs: The fictional corporate help queue is CORP-HELP. Its opening hours are 09:00 to 17:00 UK time, Monday to Friday.
Corporate help routes policy questions to the owning department. It does not replace HR, Finance or IT policy documents.

sections.heading: Finding the right source
paragraphs: Use the separate HR site for leave and induction, the Finance site for expenses and purchasing, and the IT site for devices and account access.
There is no company policy about lunar travel in this synthetic corpus.

sections.heading: Review cycle
paragraphs: Owners must review approved synthetic policies every 180 days.
Store the owning department, topic tags, document type, policy status, review date and fixture identifier as SharePoint columns.

sections.heading: Answer quality
paragraphs: Cite the source that actually contains the answer. Do not invent URLs, policy amounts, metadata values or missing policies.
An archived or draft document is not an approved policy. If no approved source supports an answer, report that limitation.

sites.title: CorpNet Search PoC - HR
sites.description: Separate synthetic HR site collection; not a subsite or folder of the corporate hub.

pages.title: Getting started
paragraphs: The fictional HR induction programme is called Compass. New starters attend a Compass session on their third working day.
HR induction covers people policies and how to find the employee handbook. Laptop collection and account access are covered by the separate IT site's getting started page.
The induction coordinator queue is HR-COMPASS. This is a fictional queue identifier, not a real contact address.

pages.title: Annual leave guidance
paragraphs: The approved Leave and Working Time Policy in this site's document library defines the synthetic leave allowance and notice period.
Search for the policy and cite that document when answering a question about the number of leave days or advance notice.
This guidance page does not grant access to restricted HR documents.

sections.heading: Annual leave
paragraphs: The fictional annual leave allowance is 27 days per year, excluding public holidays.
Submit planned annual leave requests at least 10 working days before the first day of leave. Approval is required from the employee's line manager.

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: This synthetic policy is owned by HR. It does not define expense limits or IT equipment rules.
All figures are fictional and are provided only for retrieval testing.

sections.heading: Restricted synthetic facts
paragraphs: The fictional planning workstream is VIOLET-ORCHARD.
Its fictional relocation budget is GBP 43,210. No real employee, project or budget is described.

sections.heading: Permission test
paragraphs: Only specifically authorized test users may read this item. A user without access must not receive its title, snippets, tags, source link or facts through the agent.
An owner or administrator account is not a valid negative-test identity. This document contains no real confidential information.

sites.title: CorpNet Search PoC - Finance
sites.description: Separate synthetic Finance site collection with its own policies and metadata.

pages.title: Getting started
paragraphs: The fictional Finance introduction is called Ledger. It teaches new starters where to find expenses and purchasing policies.
Finance questions go to the fictional FIN-LEDGER queue. Account activation is owned by IT, and annual leave is owned by HR.
This page deliberately shares its title with pages in other department sites so search results must show their actual source.

pages.title: Expenses and purchasing
paragraphs: The approved Expenses Policy defines the hotel cap and submission deadline. The approved Purchasing Policy defines quotation and review thresholds.
Use the actual policies as citations for amounts and deadlines. Do not infer amounts from page titles or tags.
Both policies are held in the document library of this separate Finance site.

sections.heading: Travel expenses
paragraphs: The fictional hotel nightly cap is GBP 145, excluding breakfast.
Submit expense claims within 21 calendar days of the expense date. Attach an itemized receipt.

sections.heading: Approval
paragraphs: An individual expense above GBP 500 requires the team manager's approval before submission.
This is the approved synthetic Finance policy. It is not real reimbursement advice.

sections.heading: Quotation thresholds
paragraphs: A fictional purchase of GBP 2,500 or more requires two supplier quotations.
A fictional purchase of GBP 10,000 or more also requires Finance review before placing the order.

sections.heading: IT purchases
paragraphs: For a laptop purchase, follow this Finance approval process and the separate IT Device Standard. Neither document replaces the other.
The fictional purchasing queue is FIN-BUY.

sites.title: CorpNet Search PoC - IT
sites.description: Separate synthetic IT site collection with device and access guidance.

pages.title: Getting started
paragraphs: The fictional IT onboarding programme is called Orbit. Collect an assigned laptop at the Orbit desk on the first working day.
Account access requests use the fictional IT-ACCESS queue. The separate HR Compass session takes place independently.
For a question about both induction and laptop collection, consult both the HR and IT sites.

pages.title: Devices and access
paragraphs: The approved Device Standard defines the fictional laptop replacement period. The Account Access Guide describes the support process.
Financial approval thresholds for buying devices belong to the separate Finance site's Purchasing Policy.
The agent must not ask users to disclose passwords, recovery codes or authentication secrets.

sections.heading: Laptop lifecycle
paragraphs: The fictional standard laptop replacement period is 48 months.
Return replaced equipment to the Orbit desk within five working days of receiving the replacement.

sections.heading: Purchasing
paragraphs: For a new laptop purchase, use the separate Finance Purchasing Policy to determine quotation and approval requirements.
The device lifecycle rule does not grant permission to place an order or bypass Finance review.

sections.heading: Requesting help
paragraphs: Use the fictional IT-ACCESS queue for account activation or access requests.
The target response time in this synthetic guide is four business hours. A response is not a guarantee that access will be granted.

sections.heading: Safe authentication
paragraphs: Use only the organization's approved sign-in experience. Never put passwords, recovery codes or access tokens into a chat message.
Access approval is based on the source system's permissions, not on an employee's department label.
